conviction_note: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Tupperware LatAm consolidated. The company's own filings put Q3 revenue at about Ps 4.8bn (about $272M at ~17.7 MXN/USD), against a single-source $261.4M consensus. They also put FY2026 at about +24-25% against the company's +18-22% guide, so a beat and/or a guide raise is the likely fundamental read. Three things offset it: organic margin pressure (container freight about 2.2x year on year, Jafra investment, a 21.4% EBITDA-margin Q3 2025 comp); this name selling its last revenue beat (Q2 2026 +$10M revenue beat and new guide, -3.35%); and a disputed EPS bar ($0.71 vs $0.67). So impact_sum is -0.2 and p_up is 51 on abs_move 4.5. The two measurements agree on 'near zero', and the gap between print_vs_bar (+4%) and expected move (+0.1) is deliberate: the reaction function vetoes the beat.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Tupperware LatAm consolidated: June alone booked Ps 451m revenue and Ps 123m EBITDA (27.4% margin), and pro forma FY2025 Tupperware revenue was Ps 5.09bn. Adding organic growth of ~4% (Q2 2026 organic +4.1%) to the Q3 2025 base of Ps 3,377m gives Q3 revenue of about Ps 4.75-4.85bn, or about $268-275M at a ~17.6-17.8 Q3 average rate, against the $261.4M Benzinga consensus (+3-5%). Repeated over H2, the same arithmetic puts FY2026 at about Ps 17.7-17.9bn (+24-25%), above the top of the company's own 18-22% guide (Ps 16.81-17.38bn). That makes a beat plus a guide raise, or an explicit acknowledgement that the guide is conservative, the likely content of the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23 amc): revenue beat by about $10M and a new guide of +18-22% after the acquisition; stock -3.35% (17.31 to 16.73). Q4 2025 (2026-02-26): FY2025 revenue of Ps 14.26bn missed the company's own 14.9-15.3bn guide and the 2026 guide was +4-8%; -8.8% (18.17 to 16.57). Q3 2025 (2025-10-23): EBITDA +22%, +2.85%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-23): -2.1%. Closes from Yahoo chart v8. This name has punished guide misses and has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a raise above the guide, the stock would not have drifted -4.2% over 20 days into the print on falling volume, and the H2 consensus would not sit exactly at the top of the 18-22% guide (Benzinga Q3+Q4 of about $550M, or about Ps 9.7bn) instead of above it. Coverage is 1-3 analysts and the USD consensus requires an FX assumption, so the mechanical Tupperware run-rate is easy to under-model.
findings.independence: The Tupperware run-rate also appears in the closing 6-K (Q1 2026 Tupperware revenue of US$75M, i.e. about US$300M a year: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788257/000121390026064312/ea029318101ex99-1_better.htm, 2026-06-02) and in the six-month interim financials (pro forma H1 revenue of Ps 9.66bn: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026105780/ea030695701ex99-1.htm, filed 2026-10-01). All are company documents, so they are one source family. Q3 revenue and the FY guide rest on one calculation and are filed as one finding.

findings.finding: Organic margin faces three company-confirmed or proxy headwinds against a tough comp. Q3 2025 EBITDA margin was 21.4% (Jafra Mexico adj. EBITDA +31.3%). In Q2 2026 Jafra EBITDA fell 6.7%, consolidated gross margin fell 161bp to 65.5%, and management flagged higher Betterware logistics costs from Strait of Hormuz tensions. Drewry's WCI composite was $4,500/FEU on 2026-09-17 against $1,913 on 2025-09-18 (about 2.35x), with Shanghai-LA at $7,712. Betterware imports its product, so Q3/Q4 COGS carries this. Net of Tupperware's ~27% margin, consolidated margin can still clear the at-least-19% guide, so the risk is to the organic EBITDA line and to EPS, not to the full-year margin floor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 EBITDA margin fell 30bp, with Jafra EBITDA -6.7% and the EPS consensus disputed as a miss or a beat; stock -3.35%. Q3 2025 EBITDA +22% bought +2.85%. Margin has been the line this name trades on alongside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.71 is close to a model that keeps the organic margin flat (my build: EBITDA ~Ps 1.0bn, interest ~Ps 175m on Ps 7.3bn debt, 31% tax, about Ps 12.5/share, about $0.70). It does not obviously embed a further organic margin step-down from freight. The disagreement between $0.71 and $0.67 suggests some estimates do embed it, so this is partly priced.
findings.independence: Year-ago WCI levels: https://www.mtsinsights.com/summaries/4950/ (2025-09-18, $1,913). Company-level confirmation of logistics pressure is in the Q2 2026 release (https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20594085). Freight-to-COGS transmission for Q3 is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Mexican consumer demand stayed soft into Q3. ANTAD total same-store sales were +1.7% in August 2026 and +1.5% for January-August, with self-service same-store at -0.7% in August. A September report (El CEO, 2026-10-14, per search snippet only) puts department-store same-store at -0.8% and self-service at -0.3%. Walmex Mexico same-store was +1.8% in Q2 2026, and management said its initiatives had not yet produced the expected improvement. The Q2 release also said Betterware's northern region was weaker on FX effects on consumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Betterware organic revenue grew +3.6% (Betterware) and +4.1% (organic total) in Q2 2026 in a similar retail environment; the stock fell 3.35% on that print for other reasons. There is no clean history of this line moving the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: ANTAD and Walmex are public and the 20-day drift is consistent with it. It is filed small because direct selling's catalogue channel does not track self-service retail closely.
findings.independence: Walmex 2Q26 webcast script: https://files.walmex.mx/upload/files/2026/ES/Trimestral/2T26/Walmex%20Script%20Webcast%202T26.pdf (2026-07-22). Both are retail proxies, not BeFra numbers.

findings.finding: The peso weakened at the end of the quarter. The FIX reached 18.28 MXN/USD on 2026-10-02, a level not seen since 25 November 2025, against about 17.4 implied by Q2 2026 (Ps 4,161m equals $239.3M). BeFra imports in USD and hedges forecast purchases with forwards (interim financials), so this lands mainly in Q4 cost commentary and in the USD translation of the forward guide, not in Q3 COGS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated FX reaction on record for this name; the Q2 2026 release cited FX-hit consumption in the north.

findings.why_not_priced: FX is public and largely priced. It is filed because a weaker peso into Q4 raises the bar for any margin comment on the call.

findings.finding: Shareholders met on 2026-10-16 with a single substantive agenda item, approving a dividend, and the amount has not been disclosed (the notice carries no figure). Precedent is Ps 200m (Q1 2026) then Ps 250m (Q2 2026, about $0.36/share), roughly a 9% annualised yield at Ps 250m on spot. The amount will be announced alongside or just after the release; a maintained or raised payout after the acquisition debt would confirm cash generation (FY2025 FCF Ps 2.13bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Ps 250m Q2 dividend was announced 2026-07-23 with the print (stock -3.35%); no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is unknown to the market. A cut would show on a levered name, but a cut is unlikely given 74% FCF/EBITDA in Q2 and covenant leverage of 1.74x against a 3.0x maximum.
findings.independence: Q2 dividend precedent: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260723382551/en/ (2026-07-23). Covenants: interim financials https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026105780/ea030695701ex99-1.htm.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to cut against. The fundamental read (mechanical revenue beat, likely guide raise) cuts against the 20-day drift lower, but this name sold its last revenue beat and its last guide change, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Two readings of one document: the draft's 'Q3 revenue beats $261.4M' (+0.4) and 'FY guide arithmetic implies a raise' (+0.8) rested on one Tupperware run-rate calculation, so they were merged into one guidance finding at +0.8.
Rule 6 (bar has one source for revenue, two disagreeing for EPS): the reported-quarter findings stay capped small; the merged finding is sized against the company's own guide, which is sourced.
Rule 1 (beats sold: Q2 2026 revenue beat bought -3.35%): p_up kept at 51 and the merged positive held at +0.8 rather than raised.
